verses.text: Jephthah from Gilead was a mighty warrior. His father was Gilead, and his mother was a prostitute.
Gilead's wife also gave him sons. When they grew up, they drove Jephthah away. "You will not get any share of our family's property," they said, "because you are the son of another woman."
So Jephthah ran away from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob. A group of worthless men gathered around him and went out raiding with him.
Some time later, the Ammonites went to war against Israel.
When this happened, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.
They said to him, "Come and be our commander, so we can fight the Ammonites."
Jephthah said to them, "Did you not hate me and drive me out of my father's house? Why do you come to me now, when you are in trouble?"
The elders of Gilead answered, "That is why we are turning to you now. Come with us and fight the Ammonites, and you will be head over everyone living in Gilead."
Jephthah answered, "Suppose you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them to me. Will I really be your head?"
The elders of Gilead replied, "The LORD is our witness. We will certainly do as you say."
So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their head and commander. And he repeated all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, asking, "What do you have against me, that you have come to attack my country?"

The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "When Israel came up out of Egypt, they took away my land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, all the way to the Jordan. Now give it back peacefully."
Jephthah sent messengers back to the king of the Ammonites,
saying, "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
When Israel came up out of Egypt, they went through the desert to the Red Sea and on to Kadesh.

Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let us go through your country,' but the king of Edom would not listen. They sent the same message to the king of Moab, and he refused too. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.

Next they travelled through the desert, going around the lands of Edom and Moab. They passed along the eastern side of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon. They did not go into Moab's land, because the Arnon was its border.
Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, 'Please let us pass through your country to our own place.'
But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his land. He gathered all his army, camped at Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Then the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his army into Israel's hands, and they defeated them. Israel took over all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country.
They took all of it, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the desert to the Jordan.
Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven the Amorites out ahead of his people Israel, what right do you have to take it over?
Will you not take what your god Chemosh gives you? In the same way, we will take whatever the LORD our God has given us.
Are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever argue with Israel or fight against them?
For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon, Aroer, the villages around them, and all the towns along the Arnon. Why did you not take them back during all that time?
I have not wronged you, but you are doing wrong by attacking me. Let the LORD, the Judge, decide the dispute today between the Israelites and the Ammonites."
But the king of the Ammonites paid no attention to the message Jephthah sent him.
Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jephthah. He went across Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah in Gilead, and from there went on against the Ammonites.
Jephthah made a promise to the LORD: "If you give the Ammonites into my hands,
whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I come home safely from fighting the Ammonites will belong to the LORD, and I will offer it as a burnt offering."
Then Jephthah went to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hands.
He destroyed twenty towns from Aroer to the area of Minnith, as far as Abel Keramim, in a great defeat. So the Ammonites were brought under Israel's control.
When Jephthah came home to Mizpah, who should come out to meet him but his daughter, dancing to the sound of tambourines! She was his only child. He had no other son or daughter.
When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, "Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me great sorrow and trouble, because I have made a promise to the LORD that I cannot break."
She said, "My father, you have made a promise to the LORD. Do to me what you promised, now that the LORD has paid back your enemies, the Ammonites."
Then she said, "Grant me just one request. Give me two months to wander in the hills with my friends and cry because I will never marry."
"You may go," he said. He let her go for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and cried because she would never marry.
After two months she came back to her father, and he did to her as he had promised. She had never slept with a man. From this came a custom in Israel
that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to remember the daughter of Jephthah from Gilead.
